message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's latest results and bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.80 (filled at $222.80, ~$9,803 total), which is within the $10,000 per-order cap and well under the $20,000 daily limit, with no funds moved out of the account. Apple's fiscal Q4 2024 (ended Sept 28, 2024) showed revenue of $94.9B, up 6% year over year, and full-year net sales of $391.0B with net income of $93.7B, or $6.08 diluted EPS — figures that include a one-time $10.2B income tax charge, and which I confirmed against both Apple's newsroom release and the SEC 10-K. I deliberately discarded a third-party blog claiming $416.2B revenue / $112.0B net income / $7.46 EPS, since it contradicted the primary filings. News flow was neutral-to-constructive: shares were roughly flat near $222 as investors weighed iPhone 16 demand and the gradual Apple Intelligence rollout, so I sized a modest position at a limit price essentially at the current ask ($222.72) rather than chasing. The rationale is a solid, growing franchise with a tax-charge-distorted headline EPS, bought at market with no premium paid.
